lede: Wednesday's HARC meeting is the one to watch this week: the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific Ave goes before the commission for three separate Preliminary Large-Scale public hearings covering multiple new buildings in Backman Village — the kind of project that will reshape a corner of town for a long time. The same day, the Board of County Commissioners takes up two Land Use Code amendments, including new rules for natural medicine businesses and nonconforming lots, both of which have real consequences for what gets built and where across the county. San Miguel County also holds its sixth housing code working session Thursday, pushing toward final recommendations on zoning, density, and workforce housing incentives.

notable.stake: HARC votes on alterations to two Town-owned landmark civic buildings.
Carhenge redevelopment: three public hearings on large-scale new construction in Backman Village.
BOCC considers Land Use Code amendments on natural medicine businesses and nonconforming lots.
